definition: Mutation Execution Reliability = % of attempted mutation executions producing a valid authoritative result without infrastructure ambiguity.

primary_failure_modes: F002: import path failure (resolved in C42.16)
F006: CI path bug (resolved in C42.25)
F013: CI timeout on full campaign

target_reliability_threshold.rationale: A system with high mutation score but poor execution reliability is not trustworthy. The 95% floor ensures that at least 19 of 20 execution attempts produce valid results.

new_architecture_improvements.isolated_workspace: Eliminates F004 (source reversion), F005 (config contamination), F011 (dirty tree cache issues)
new_architecture_improvements.canonical_cache: Eliminates F003 (stale cache reuse) by fingerprint-based invalidation
new_architecture_improvements.correctness_gate: Eliminates F008/F014 (invalid execution misclassified as SURVIVED)
new_architecture_improvements.sharding: Eliminates F013 (CI timeout) by splitting campaigns into sub-timeout shards
new_architecture_improvements.explicit_timeout: Distinguishes TIMEOUT from EXECUTION_ERROR (F009 partial fix)

projected_reliability.confidence: derived from elimination of 5 of 16 historical failure modes
remaining_risks: F007: mutmut silent skip of Python 3.12+ syntax (structural limitation of libcst backend)
F012: flaky tests with global state (test-suite limitation, not architecture)
F015: environment drift between local/CI (requires lock-file discipline)
